final.memo:
Charlie and I have looked at this business and concluded that it sits firmly outside our circle of competence. While the company operates as a toll bridge for data traffic, it functions in a field defined by rapid technological change and significant substitution risks [D01, D05, D06].

We require businesses with a durable competitive advantage and a predictable record of returns on capital. Here, however, the need for continuous engineering investment and an aggressive acquisition strategy makes it impossible to assess the true owner earnings of the enterprise [D01, D03, D05].

The market is currently valuing this business at an extreme multiple of 131x to 212x earnings [D04]. Such a valuation ignores the reality that even a wonderful business becomes a poor investment if the price paid is detached from economic reality [D04, D05].

We prefer to hold cash rather than deploy it into speculative assets where we cannot confidently estimate intrinsic value. We will continue to wait for opportunities where we can buy a wonderful business at a fair price [D08].
